title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: datavana service based precomposed prompts different workflows. can override default prompt templates -pass post-processing get direct LLM answers using llm_prompt() function. Provide prompts prompt.user- prompt.system-parameters. prompts, case input data frame df, placeholder {{text}} replaced content selected abstract column. Note: previous example, used paste0() concatenate sentences. serves readability, alternatively, can provide prompt one single character string.
code: # Submit tasks results <- llm_prompt(   df, abstract,      prompt.system = paste0(     "Output a comma separated list of categories. ",     "Just the list, nothing else. ",     "The possible categories are: scifi, historical, drama, comedy, fantasy, romance"   ),      prompt.user = "{{text}}"    )   # Fetch results results <- llm_prompt(custom)

what: Adapt prompts for the existing workflow methods
title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: Instead using llm_prompt()-function, can also adapt prompts used workflow-specific functions llm_summarize(), llm_code() llm_annotate(). Using technique, can leverage pre- post-processing steps Databoard service. example, providing rules, result automatically split one field category. way: hood, llm_prompt() function uses summary workflow settings simply disable result processing. prompt templates, use {{text}} placeholder define slot content data frame inserted. {{rules}} placeholder replaced markdown formatted list rules provided rules book. using rules, make sure prompt compatible expected pattern. post-processing procedure expects one line output column. whatever follows category name inserted column. enter line breaks prompt, use escape sequence \n.
code:
results <- llm_summarize(   movies, abstract, rules,       options = list(       prompts = list(         system = paste0(           "You are an expert in content analysis. Be precise and concise.",           "Use the codebook provided to decide for each category, ",           "whether the given text falls into the category. ",                      "Return one line for each category. ",           "Each returned line must start with the category name ",            "followed by a colon ':' and then followed by one of the codes ",                      "'5' if the category applies fully, ",           "'4' if the category mostly applies, ",           "'3' if the category partially applies, ",            "'2' if the category mostly does not apply, ",           "'1' if the category does not apply at all. ",                       "Return only the lines for each category - ",           "nothing else, no introduction, no explanation, no disclaimer!
",                      "# Rules:
 {{rules}}
"         ),         user = "{{text}}"      )    ) )  results <- llm_summarize(results)

text: service designed called multiple times gather results irrespective wait time. first submit jobs poll results finished. wait parameter describes time seconds service waits result LLM request (default = 0, values range 0 10). typical use cases, default zero sensible choice. data set small know answers available fast, can increase wait time lucky, results available directly submitting tasks:

title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: workflows can return multiple values per case, example coding text multiple categories summarizing text multiple rules. llm_code() exposes explicit mode argument. controls coding result structured: single (default): return single best-matching category per case. multi: return one value per category, 2 means category strongly applies, 1 means applies, 0 means apply. llm_summarize() method uses idea internally, switches automatically: rules returns one result per rule, otherwise returns single summary per case. typical use case multi-mode extracting information movie’s year, topic main character’s name. Example:
code: # Single mode (default)  results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules, mode = "single") results <- llm_code(results)  # Multi mode  results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules, mode = "multi") results <- llm_code(results) rules <- tibble::tribble(   ~category,  ~description,                                  ~example,   "figure",   "The names of the main characters in the movie", "John Doe",   "gender",   "The gender of the main characters",             "male" )  results <- llm_summarize(df, abstract, rules) results <- llm_summarize(results)

title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: workflow wrappers forward model-related settings via options list. common ones : model: choose LLM model use. temperature: control deterministic varied answer . See databoard API documentation complete list available options values. set options, server defaults used. example:
code: results <- llm_code(   df, abstract, rules,       options = list(     model = 'mistral-small',     temperature = "0.2"   ) )  results <- llm_code(results)

title: Getting started with the databoard
text: Datavana Databoard service can easily feed content LLM automated analyses.´ submitted tasks, data processed background. Therefore, working service, always implies two-step procedure. Firstly, submit tasks let service work. Secondly, retrieve results. R package wraps main functions service: llm_summarize() used condense text shorter paragraphs even single words. provide categories, one summary keyword returned category. llm_code() assigns predefined categories text. Provide codebook category names, descriptions, optionally examples. Depending settings, workflow return one multiple matching categories. llm_annotate() adds -text annotations, example, extract person place names. According rule set, matching text segments enclosed XML tags. predefined methods based pre-composed prompt templates include pre- post-processing steps aligned workflow. can customize prompts several options exposed service. gain full flexibility, use custom prompts -pass processing steps: llm_prompt() fetches LLM answers using prompt templates.

title: Automated content summarisation with an LLM — llm_summarize
text: data data frame containing texts summarised, data frame previously returned llm_summarize() whose pending results fetched. col column data holding input text. Tidy-evaluation supported (pass bare column name). rules Optional. Provide rules produce multiple summaries. data frame columns category, description, example. One output created category. description prompt summarize. Optionally, add example expected output. options named list additional options passed Databoard server. wait Integer. Seconds wait server-side per case task complete returning. 0 (default): submit tasks return immediately state PENDING. Fetch results later calling llm_summarize(data) . > 0: wait many seconds per case result.

title: Automated content summarisation with an LLM — llm_summarize
text: function two modes operation, dispatched automatically: Submit — data yet contain .task_id column, texts col submitted new summarisation tasks (via da_submit()). Fetch — data already contains .task_id column (.e. previously returned llm_summarize()), function fetches results tasks still pending (via da_fetch()). case, parameters ignored. Typical usage call llm_summarize() submit, call repeatedly returned data frame results (see da_finished()). customize prompts, provide options:   prompts given character vectors, elements collapsed using line break (llm_prompt()). present prompts, placeholder {{text}} replaced value current case. placeholder {{rules}} replaced rule book generated rules data frame. See databoard documentation options.
